text:
This bigger picture POV from @grok is interesting.

The legal change is simple. Australia is expanding eSafety’s power so the Commissioner can demand information and documents from “a person” if there are reasonable grounds to think that person holds material relevant to the under-16 social media ban, or to whether a service even counts as an age-restricted platform. That person can be a platform, an age-assurance vendor, a contractor, or an individual. There is no trade-secret carve-out. Notices can be issued to people and companies outside Australia. Non-compliance with the notice is a civil penalty of about $364,000 for an individual. The platform-level fine for failing the age rule itself is far larger, up to about $99 million.

That is the mechanism. The rest is what it can be used for.

What it can reach

It is not a general warrant over every website. It is tied to age-restricted social media and the systems used to keep under-16s off accounts. In practice that covers the major platforms and the vendors that supply their age checks. Internal systems, policies, emails, test results, architecture notes, and vendor methods can all be “relevant.” A random bank or shop with an age gate is generally outside it. A YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, or their age-check supplier is inside it.

Google being contracted through Ireland does not end the problem. The Australian notice can still go to the provider of the Australian-facing service. The documents and the people who know the systems may sit in the US, Ireland, or both. Ireland adds GDPR and conflict-of-law friction. It is not a shield.

The real threat, worst case

Assume a future Australian government that wants the power used hard, not sparingly. Then the statute allows:

Compelling platforms and vendors to hand over proprietary age-assurance methods and internal compliance files.
Naming individual engineers or administrators who work on those systems and requiring them to produce documents and give information they have from that role.
Using “reasonable grounds” as a low first-instance test set by the regulator, with court review only after the demand exists.
Issuing those notices to people who are not in Australia.
Pressuring the platform if a vendor or employee refuses, because refusal becomes evidence that the platform cannot prove “reasonable steps.”

What it still cannot do, even then: lawfully demand unrelated personal files, dump an entire company, or physically seize machines abroad. A notice to a US person with no Australian assets is also hard to collect. The danger is not magic remote access. It is legal compulsion plus commercial leverage against firms that need the Australian market, plus the possibility of targeting named technical staff.

Why the US interest is real

This is extra-territorial compulsion of US companies, US-held trade secrets, and potentially US persons. That is a different problem from “Australia may regulate platforms that sell into Australia.” Market-access regulation is common. A foreign regulator using a broad “any person” clause to reach US employees and vendor internals is the part that should concern Washington.

Safeguards the US should put in place

These are defensive measures against abuse of a foreign civil power, not a claim about the current Australian government.

A clear blocking rule for US persons. US law should say that an Australian information notice cannot, by itself, compel a US individual or US-incorporated entity to produce documents or testimony located in the United States. Compliance would require a US court order or a recognised government-to-government channel.

Treat proprietary technical material as a protected class. Age-assurance models, system architecture, source, keys, and internal test data should not be exportable to a foreign regulator unless a US authority has reviewed the request for necessity, minimisation, and the risk of later misuse.

Do not enforce these notices in US courts as a default. Foreign civil penalties and production orders against US residents should not be collected here unless they meet a high comity test: narrow scope, no fishing, no targeting of individuals who are mere employees, and no demand for secrets unrelated to a specific, evidenced compliance question.

Separate the platform from the employee. If Australia wants records, the demand should go to the company. The US should refuse to treat a named sysadmin as the proper target of a foreign civil notice.

Conflict-of-law protocol with Ireland and the EU. Because the records may sit in Google Ireland or another EU entity, the US should coordinate with Irish/EU authorities so a company is not punished by Australia for obeying GDPR, or punished by Europe for obeying Australia.

Transparency trigger. Any foreign demand for US technical staff or core systems should have to be notified to the US government. Silent compliance by a company under market pressure is how extra-territorial powers grow.

Reciprocity test. The US should ask whether it would accept an Australian official compelling a US engineer on US soil, or a US vendor in California, on a “reasonable grounds” letter. If the answer is no, the safeguard should match that answer.

The clean line is this: Australia can set rules for services offered to Australians. It should not acquire, through a broad production power, a standing ability to reach into US companies’ internals and US individuals’ work product. The bill’s wording is wide enough that a future hostile government would not need a new law to try. It would only need to use this one without restraint. That is the threat. The US safeguard is to make unreviewed compliance with that kind of notice legally and practically difficult.

They gathered at the Sun as the daylight died,
With shovels in their hands and their facts pushed aside.
They dug to the left and they dug to the right,
Then blamed Mark Carney when Trump picked the fight.

They did the Maple MAGA Mash!
They did the graveyard bash!
They dug a Conservative crash!
They did the Maple MAGA Mash!

Trump slapped on tariffs — “Well, Canada’s to blame!”
Trump moved the goalposts — “Carney lost the game!”
Trump eyed our dollar — “Perhaps we should bend!”
Trump wanted more power over deals that we penned.

Dig, dig, dig — boys, deeper you go!
There’s always more Canada you can throw below.
Economics? Science? Evidence? Facts?
Just grab another shovel and bury all that!

Then out of the darkness stepped James Moore,
Harper’s own Industry Minister from before.
No Liberal partisan, no Carney man—
A senior Conservative who understands:

When Washington offers a terrible deal,
Walking away can be strength made real.
You don’t save your country by crawling along,
And signing a bad deal doesn’t make the deal strong.

But they dug the Maple MAGA Mash!
They dug with ideological flash!
Every Trump demand became Canada’s bash—
So they dug the Conservative crash!

And that’s what’s so strange about this whole affair:
Whatever Trump does, Canada’s somehow to bear.
He threatens our companies, our trade and our say,
And certain Canadian pundits shout, “Give more away!”

What kind of conservatism conserves none of this?
Our sovereignty, industry, leverage dismissed?
You can dislike Carney. You can paint the town blue.
But shouldn’t Canada come before your ideology too?

Yet shovel by shovel and column by column,
They keep digging downward, increasingly solemn.
Not because Canadians suddenly turned Liberal red—
But because some Conservatives can’t get this through their heads:

You don’t build a movement by cheering the shove
Of a foreign president against the country you love.
You don’t win back voters by demanding they see
That surrender to Trump is good strategy.

So dig, boys, dig! Keep digging that hole!
Put ideology first and surrender control.
Because if Trump comes first and Canada comes last,
You’re not burying Carney—

You’re burying the Conservative Party fast.

🚨 FACT-CHECK: NO EVIDENCE TINUBU FACES ARREST IN NEW YORK — EVEN VON BATTEN’S FIRM REJECTS THE CLAIM

By Ishola Adebiyi | The Trojan Beast

A dramatic narrative has been circulating around Nigerian political social media: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu will supposedly be arrested by American authorities if he travels to New York for the United Nations General Assembly.

There is one major problem.

No publicly available U.S. government or federal court record currently establishes such an arrest plan.

And now, even Von Batten-Montague-York—the lobbying firm aggressively campaigning against Tinubu and publicising allegations concerning his past—has pushed back against the arrest narrative.

The firm stated that claims suggesting Tinubu would be arrested during UNGA were untrue.

That distinction matters.

FOIA CASE ≠ CRIMINAL PROSECUTION

Much of the speculation appears to arise from ongoing litigation in the United States concerning access to government records associated with Tinubu.

But a Freedom of Information Act lawsuit is a records-disclosure proceeding.

It does not automatically mean that the subject of those records has been criminally charged, indicted or placed under an arrest warrant.

Those are completely different legal processes.

As things stand, no publicly identified federal indictment, arrest warrant, DOJ announcement or FBI statement has been produced showing that American authorities intend to arrest President Tinubu in New York.

ALLEGATIONS ARE NOT ARREST WARRANTS

There is another important distinction being lost online.

Von Batten's organisation has made numerous political and lobbying claims concerning Tinubu, Washington and the United States government.

Those statements should be reported for what they are: claims by a private lobbying and advocacy organisation.

They are not automatically statements from the White House, FBI, Department of Justice, State Department or a U.S. federal court.

Even an allegation about someone's historical conduct does not establish that a current criminal prosecution exists.

THE $3 MILLION CLAIM ALSO NEEDS EVIDENCE

Another allegation now circulating deserves the same evidentiary standard.

Von Batten-Montague-York has alleged that someone connected to Tinubu offered the firm $3 million to abandon its campaign.

That is a serious allegation.

But until independently authenticated communications, financial records, sworn testimony, court filings or findings from competent U.S. authorities establish what happened, the responsible description remains:

The lobbying firm alleges that an offer was made.

It is not presently responsible to convert that allegation into the statement:

“Tinubu offered Von Batten $3 million.”

Those are not the same claim.

TROJAN BEAST VERDICT

🔴 CLAIM: Tinubu will be arrested when he arrives in New York.

VERDICT: UNSUBSTANTIATED.

There is presently no publicly established U.S. arrest warrant, indictment or law-enforcement announcement supporting that claim.

🟡 CLAIM: Tinubu or his associates offered Von Batten's firm $3 million.

VERDICT: ALLEGATION — NOT INDEPENDENTLY ESTABLISHED.

The burden remains on whoever makes the allegation to produce evidence capable of independent authentication.

Political excitement cannot substitute for documentation.

And a FOIA lawsuit cannot magically become a criminal indictment because social media says so.

If an arrest warrant exists, produce the warrant.
If an indictment exists, produce the indictment.
If the FBI announced an arrest, produce the FBI statement.

Until then, an allegation remains an allegation.

The United States is importing record volumes of copper from the Democratic Republic of Congo as American industrial buyers increasingly turn to the African producer for cheaper supplies.

US imports of Congolese copper cathodes reached a record 53,290 metric tonnes in July 2026, according to trade data cited by Reuters. That gave the DRC a 23.9% share of total US copper imports for the month.

The scale of the increase is striking. The United States imported less than 32,000 tonnes of copper from the DRC during the whole of 2024, meaning July 2026 alone exceeded that annual total.

American manufacturers, including copper rod mills and tube producers, are increasingly accepting Congolese copper because it can be significantly cheaper than brands approved for delivery on the US COMEX exchange.

Reuters reports that Congolese copper has recently been offered at discounts of around $550 to $800 per tonne compared with COMEX-approved material.

No Congolese copper brand is currently approved for delivery on COMEX. Among African producers, only two Zambian brands are listed on the exchange.

The shift also comes as the DRC increases copper production and as traders move metal into the United States ahead of possible tariffs.

At the same time, China remains the DRC’s biggest copper customer, but Chinese imports from Congo fell by 4.3% in the first seven months of 2026.

The new trade figures point to growing US demand for one of the DRC’s most important mineral exports at a time when Washington and Beijing are competing more openly for access to Africa’s critical minerals.

For Kinshasa, the trend could offer an opportunity to diversify its export markets beyond China, although the country remains heavily dependent on raw mineral exports and foreign processing capacity.

text:
Came across this argument that Genesis 14 foreshadows Armageddon. The person making this is a historicist, although I'm not sure that matters for this argument, which is laid out as follows:

Genesis 14 is the first place in Scripture where Armageddon is presented in type in astonishing detail. The record covers the period from Armageddon to the full establishment of the Kingdom when Christ will share a fellowship meal with his saints in the House of Prayer for all nations.

The Battle of the Kings: The first cameo of the Kingdom
Verse 1A northern confederacy forms—“In the days of these kings”—Dan. 2:44
Verses 2-7Northern confederacy invades the Land—Gog foreshadowed.
Verses 8-12Southern confederacy defeated—Lot and family taken captive
Verses 13-16Abraham meets Melchizedek king of Salem—Fellowship.
Verses 21-24Abraham repudiates the king of Sodom’s offer of wealth

Vs. 1: ‘And it came to pass in the days.’ Cp. Dan. 2:44. Nebuchadnezzar’s image is prefigured here in the 4 kings who form this confederacy.

‘Amraphel.’ “One that speaks of secrets” (Hitchcock); “Keeper of the gods” (Smith); “powerful people” (Youngs). After defeating Arioch he united Babylonia under one rule, and made Babylon his capital.

‘Shinar.’ “Two rivers” (DBD, Smith, Fausset). Hebrew form of the Akkadian name Semiramis (wife of Nimrod)—the first “mother of harlots.”

‘Arioch.’ “Venerable” (Smith; “Lion-like” (DBD, Easton). Also said to mean “Servant of the moon god.”

‘Ellasar.’ “Revolting from God” (Hitchcock). Larsa in Chaldea.

“Chedorlaomer.’ “Handful of sheaves” (DBD, Smith). Thought to mean “Servant of Lagomer” an Elamite goddess) in the original language.

‘Elam.’ “Eternity” (DBD, Smith)—related to olam. East of Babylon.

‘Tidal.’ “Fear” or “reverence” (Ges.); “Great son” (DBD, Smith).

‘Nations.’ Goyim—nations; i.e. local tribes east of Tigris and north of Elam.

Prefigures Nebuchadnezzar’s Image: The 4 kings of the northern confederacy typify the 4 world empires of Dan. 2 which are to be formed into one massive image empire in the latter days. This can only be completed when Gog is victorious in the Land for Israel was part of all four empires. The head (thinking power) of the image will be “Babylon the great”; hence Amraphel is first named, although he does not lead the actual invasion.

Vs. 2: ‘Bera.’ “Son of evil (DBD, Easton, Smith).

‘Sodom.’ “Burning”. Named for its ultimate fate.

‘Birsha.’ “with iniquity (DBD); “Son of godlessness (Smith).

‘Gomorrah.’ “Submersion” (DBD, Smith, Easton).

‘Shinab.’ “Splendor of the father (DBD); “A father has turned” (Strong).

‘Adama.’ “Earthly”, “Red earth.”

‘Shemeber.’ “Lofty flight” (DBD); “Soaring on high” (Easton).

‘Zeboiim.’ “Gazelles.”

‘Bela.’ “To devour at a gulp” (Strong, Easton); “Destruction” (DBD, Smith).

‘Zoar.’ “Little”—Cp. Gen. 19:20-22.

The five kings of the south typify the corrupt latter day Tarshish powers who oppose Gog’s invasion but are defeated and humiliated in the Land. It is noteworthy that 1st World War British Empire posters listed Australia, Canada, India and New Zealand as allies—a total of 5 ‘kings.’

Vs. 3: ‘The vale of Siddim.’ “Field” or “plain”(BDB). “The valley of the open fields” (Roth.).

‘The salt sea.’ i.e. when Moses wrote after the judgments.

Vs. 4: ‘Thirteenth.’ The number of rebellion.

Vs. 5: ‘Fourteenth.’ 2x7 (covenant)=enforced covenant.

‘Rephaims.’ “Giants.” A race of giants like Og (Deut. 3”11,13; Josh. 12:4) East of Jordan.

‘Ashteroth Karnaim.’ “The horned Astartes” (Ges.).

‘Zuzims.’ “Prominent: (Strong). Giants between Amon and Jabbok—Deut. 2:20.

‘Emims.’ “Terrors,” “terrible ones.” Inhabitants of Moab—Due. 2:10.

‘Shaveh Kiriathaim.’ “Plain of double city.” See Josh. 13:19; Duet. 3:13

Vs. 6: ‘Horites.’ “Cave dwellers” in Petra.

‘Elparan.’ “The terebinth (oak) or the Plain of Paran.”

Vs. 7: ‘Enmishpat.’ “Fountain of judgment” (Ges.).

‘Kadesh.’ “Sanctuary.”

‘The country of the Amalekites.’ I.e. the country later inhabited by the Amalekites, descendants of Esau—Gen. 36:12.

‘Amorites.’ “Highlanders,” “hill-men.” Inhabitants of Canaan.

‘Hazezontamar.’ “Pruning (or dividing) of palm trees” (Easton)—the old name for Engedi—2 Chron. 20:2.

Armageddon: Hebrew derivation—3 words—aremah/gai/dan or dun. “A heap of sheaves”—aremah—heap, pile; (Strong adds—Specifically a sheaf). This word is rendered “bringing in sheaves” (Neh. 13:15); “heap of corn” (Ruth 3:7); etc. Root-aram—to heap up, pile, be heaped up. Another word rendered “sheaves” is amar—to bind sheaves; to gather.
“Valley”—gai—valley, a steep valley, narrow gorge.
“For judgment”—diyn/dun—to judge, contend, plead.

Vs. 8: ‘And there went out.’ “Thus then went forth.” (Roth.).

‘Joined the battle.’ “Set themselves in array against them for the battle” (Roth.). Same word “battle” Zech. 20:2.

‘The vale of Siddim.’ “The valley of the open fields” (Roth.).

Vs. 9: ‘Four kings with five.’ Total 9=finality/judgment.

Vs. 10: ‘Slimepits.’ Beer chemar—pit of bitumen. Root chamar—to glow with redness; boil up. Translated “red”, “troubled,” “foul” (Job 16:16).

Vs. 11: ‘Victuals.’ Okel—food.

Vs. 12: ‘Who dwelt in.’ Lit. “and he was living in.” A further step from Gen. 13:12.

‘And his goods.’ Contrast Gen. 19:12-16—God left them behind.

Vs. 13: ‘Escaped.’ Palet—a refugee. Used Jud. 12:4-5; Isa. 45:20. Type—Zech. 14:2.

‘Hebrew.’ “Cross over” (to be on the opposite side by transition). Descendants of Eber—Gen. 10:21,25.

‘Plain.’ “ Elon-Oak

‘Mamre.’ “Strength” or “fatness.”

‘Eshcol.’ “Cluster of grapes.”

‘Aner.’ “Boy.”

‘Confederate.’ Baalim berith—owners of a covenants. “Having a covenant” (Roth.). Gentiles converted by preaching the Gospel—Gal. 3:8.

Aberaham spend 20 years in Hebron. During this time his household grew to include 318 born in the camp. Added to this a number of Gentiles were converted by the preach of the “gospel” (Gal. 3:8) God had earlier revealed to him.

Gentiel converts in the army of Abram: Aner, Eschol, and Mamre all went with Abram, to the battle and were compensated for their out of pocket expenses—verse 24.

Vs. 14: ‘Brother.’ Ach—relative; kinsman.

‘Armed.’ Ruq—Empty out; pour forth. “Drew forth” (Roth.).

‘Trained.’ Chaniyk—Initiated, practiced; i.e. in matters of the Truth.

‘Dan.’ “Judgment”

Vs. 15: ‘Divided.’ Chalaq—separated by lot, see use Job 38:24 (“parted”).

‘Himself.’ Operated as one body. Cp. “he and his servants”—a type of Christ.

‘Hobah.’ “Hiding place.” 50 miles north of Damascus.

‘Left hand.’ I.e. North (to one facing east). Signifies judgment—Ps. 75:6-8.

‘Damascus.’ “Sack of blood.” Another indicator of judgment.

Vs. 16: ‘And his goods.’ Lot given opportunity to forsake Sodom, but goods prevailed in his family.

Vs. 17: ‘Went out to meet him.’ Thus acknowledging Abram as his deliverer in humility.

‘Shaveh.’ “Level plain”; root to level; equalize; resemble, hence, to be made like. Cp. Heb. 7:3—“made like unto the son of God.”

‘The king’s dale.’ Lit. “the valley of the king”; namely, Melchizedek. Note—2 Sam. 18:18; 1 Kings 1:33-34; Nehemiah 2:14-15.

Vs. 18: ‘Melchizedek.’ “King of righteousness”—Heb. 7:2. 11 occurrences in Scripture (2 OT, 9 NT all in Hebrews). 11=incompleteness. Shadow inferior to substance.

‘Salem.’ “Peace.” Jerusalem’s (“vision of peace”) name in the Kingdom—Ps. 76:2.

‘Bread and wine.’ The tokens of the New (Abrahamic) Covenant—Matt. 26:26-28.

‘The most high.’ Elyon—Elevation, lofty, supreme. Root halah—to ascend.

‘God.’ El—strength, mighty. Title of Deity as prime mover of Creation.

David later emulated Melchizedek and acted as a king and priest distributing bread and wine to both Jew and Gentile, and male and female when bringing the Ark to Zion to be placed in “the tabernacle of David”—2 Sam. 6:14-19.

Vs. 19: ‘He blessed him.’ Melchizedek greater than Abram—Heb. 7:7. See Acts 3:25-26.

‘Possessor.’ Qanah—found, create, thus to possess, own. See use Ps. 139:13; Prov. 8:22.

‘Heaven and earth.’ Armageddon will ultimately unite heaven and earth (Matt. 6:10) by revealing its true possessor.

Vs. 20: ‘Delivered.’ Magan—to shield, encompass wit. Its root is magen used Gen. 15:1 “shield.”

‘Gave him tithes of all.’ See Heb. 7:4-10.

Acts 3:25-26: Shows Abrahams’s blessing is to have the work of Christ become truly effective in turning believers from iniquity.

Vs. 21: ‘Give me.’ King sin is only interest in ruling the bodies of men.

‘Person.’ Nephesh—a breathing creature.

Vs. 22: ‘I have lift up mine hand.’ To make an oath—Ex. 6:8; Deut. 32:40 (cp. context vs. 32, 41-44, 50)

Vs. 23: ‘Thread.’ Chuwt—to sew; a string. I.w. a tie for a girl’s hair.

‘Shoelatchet.’ Serowk—a thong (as tied), and na’alah—a sandal tongue. Thus repudiates the smallest property of both male and female.

‘That is thine.’ Knew king of Sodom did not acknowledge El Elyan as “possessor of heaven and earth.”

Vs. 24: ‘Save only that which the young men have eaten.’ I.e. recover out of pocket expenses. 

‘Men.’ Enosh—weak mortal men.

‘Let them take their portion.’ Principle—1 Tim. 5:18. But they may not have done so—1 Cor. 9:4, 6-12.

She’s always pleaded not guilty. Facts and Massachusetts law below:

-The DA charged first-degree murder and stayed there. 

-A grand jury later indicted three first-degree murders. That proceeding is secret and one-sided: only the prosecution presents evidence. 

-After the grand jury indicted her, she pleaded not guilty. Massachusetts has no “I plead NGRI” box. You plead not guilty, then raise lack of criminal responsibility at trial.

-She stayed not guilty at trial and raised lack of criminal responsibility. That puts the burden on the Commonwealth: prove the crime and prove she was responsible.

-With the DA refusing to move off murder 1, LCR (lack of criminal responsibility) was the only workable route left to beat that charge.

-Reddington motioned to bifurcate: acts first, responsibility second.

-The judge denied the motion.

-Then Reddington offered a stipulation: we will not fight that her alleged actions caused the deaths if the case can focus on responsibility.

-That is not a guilty plea to murder. It is conceding alleged causation, not first-degree guilt.

-He asked for a Bowden instruction (bad police work can create reasonable doubt). Prosecutors objected. There is no clear public report that the judge gave the formal Bowden charge.

-Reddington could still argue the investigation was deficient, and he did so in the defense closing.

-Under the law, she never pleaded guilty and never formally admitted that she committed the act of murder. 

In the eyes of the law, Lindsay did not confess to the murders. The law does not treat “what she reported remembering” and “I am guilty of murder” as the same thing. They are treated differently because a crime is not just a physical event. Murder requires proof that she did the act and that the law can blame her for it. Once LCR was raised, that burden stayed on the Commonwealth.

text:
In the primary I liked checking the printed BMD ballot and feeding it into the scanner myself. Your fix is even simpler: drop every paper ballot into a locked box, let a public counting board open it and tally by hand first, then run the machines only to confirm. Nevada regs already allow a county to do exactly that sequence if it wants.

Mail ballots (the bulk of the vote) can be processed and tabulated starting 15 days before Election Day. In-person ballots get imaged and totaled the second you insert them. A full manual first-count of every ballot on Election Night itself would blow past current staffing, timelines, and the statute that lets early tabulation happen.

I would offer a change to the statute so no ballot—mail or in-person—is tabulated before Election Day. Every paper stays in a sealed box until the polls close. Counting boards open the boxes in public, do the official first count by hand, and use scanners only as a check. One uniform, observable process finished that night.

Another change to the statute would require mail ballots to be received by Election Day so they could be counted with the rest of them, rather than waiting for mail ballots to come in dribs and drabs while the rest of the nation finishes the real job.

text:
Joe Perry was a fisher of men. Someone who never missed an opportunity to share the Gospel with others and lead people to Christ. And, as importantly, to encourage and motivate other believers to do the same. The stories are many, like playing rounds of golf with foursomes of people he didn’t know and who didn’t know Jesus. He also had a huge heart for kids. And in that heart, God planted a seed to develop a program to use sports as a platform to reach the youth. That became the Prestonwood Sports Organization (PSO), founded over 26 years ago as the first ministry of its kind in America, which now serves over 5,000 boys and girls and their families each year with the message of the gospel and to develop followers of Jesus.

The first time Joe ever reached out to me was in 2010 when he wanted to make an introductory video for his son Caleb who was scheduled to speak at the end of year PSO sports gathering. Caleb was an all-district and all-area football standout at Arlington High School and was the 1997 Texas Christian Athlete of the Year before heading off to play on the offensive line at the University of Arkansas. Photographing high school and college sports wouldn’t happen until the middle of that decade for me, but you could say that that video was my first ever documenting of an athlete.

Joe would periodically ask for my help over the next several years, and with Azadeh we also worked to develop the Persian Ministry with him. Joe’s grandkids were still young at this time, but it was pretty much a given that when they came of high school age we would take in a game together. But on October 22, 2018, while on a trip to see Caleb coach as the offensive coordinator at Hewitt-Trussville High School in Alabama, Joe suddenly was called home to be with the Lord. His race here was finished, but his enormous legacy lives on.

Several years went by and his wife Linda would keep us updated on the grandkids, all of whom are exceptionally talented and athletic. In 2020, Caleb became the head coach at Bauxite High School in Arkansas, where his kids are now excelling in athletics at Bauxite Middle and High School. Two years ago, we made arrangements to take in a football game during his son Eli’s sophomore year, only for him to break his leg early in the season. A second attempt last year was intercepted by the tearing of an ACL in his knee. Praying for complete healing and protection, the third time became the charm as we were finally able to connect up north last Friday to witness Bauxite take on, and beat, rival Glen Rose in their season opener.

It was pure Friday Night Lights magic. The best that small town high school football has to offer.

The only thing missing was Joe.

Have you not known? Have you not heard? The Lord is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not faint or grow weary; his understanding is unsearchable. He gives power to the faint, and to him who has no might he increases strength. Even youths shall faint and be weary, and young men shall fall exhausted; but they who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles; they shall run and not be weary; they shall walk and not faint. Isaiah 40:28-31

🚨UPDATE: Unsettling New Context Emerges in the Barrett “Bear” Walsh Case 

​As more details come to light surrounding the tragedy of 2-year-old Barrett “Bear” Walsh, the situation grows increasingly complex and distressing.

​Information recently shared by individuals close to the family offers new insights. These details stem from family accounts rather than official court records or police reports, but they provide critical context into the days leading up to the incident and the sequence of events on September 1.

​Clarification on the Timeline of Discovery

​Recent accounts clarify the initial discovery at the Walsh residence:

​The Bus Stop Arrival: A neighbor brought the older children home from the bus stop and found the youngest child downstairs unattended.

​The Medical Response: Rather than performing CPR herself, the neighbor alerted a nearby relative who is a registered nurse.

​The Scene Inside: The nurse entered the home, discovered Barrett, and immediately initiated CPR. Upon the arrival of emergency first responders, she went upstairs and located Corie.

​Home Life and Surrounding Circumstances

​People close to Corie Walsh consistently describe her as a devoted, loving, and highly involved mother who went out of her way for her children. Family members report having no prior indication of self-harm or signs warning of what occurred.

​However, details regarding the family's daily routine highlight significant demands:

​Extended Travel: Corie’s husband, Michael, reportedly traveled frequently for work, sometimes for weeks at a time, leaving Corie to manage four young children including an infant and a toddler largely on her own.

​Behavioral Dynamics: Relatives note that Barrett was deeply attached to his father and often struggled with disruption to his routine when Michael was away, occasionally resisting meals and sleep. While notable, a child's normal behavioral challenges never shift accountability away from the adult caregiver.

​External Support: Though Corie had local family who regularly assisted, it remains unclear whether anyone was aware of the extent of her internal strain.

​The Lindsay Clancy Connection & Unanswered Questions

​Another troubling aspect involves reports that Corie was following the Lindsay Clancy trial and actively discussing it in a group text just hours before Barrett was found.

​It is currently unknown whether this detail bears any direct connection to the tragedy, or if it points to an acute mental health crisis, an impulsive act, or an underlying issue. Establishing these facts will require formal investigation and verified evidence.

​A Complex Perspective on a Devastating Loss

​Parenting multiple young children without continuous support is an extraordinary burden that can leave anyone feeling overwhelmed and exhausted. Recognizing that strain is a human response, but it must be paired with the reality that help must be sought whether from family, friends, or emergency services before reaching a point of critical failure.

​Above all, the focus remains on the victim. A 2-year-old boy lost his life, leaving behind grieving siblings, a devastated father, extended family, and neighbors and first responders tasked with processing an unthinkable trauma.

​Please keep the family, loved ones, and community in your thoughts. May Barrett “Bear” Walsh rest in peace. 

​Key Background & Official Case Facts

​The Incident: On Tuesday afternoon, September 1, 2026, emergency personnel responded to a 911 call at the Walsh family home in Frankfort, Illinois.  
​Discovery of Barrett: Barrett was found unresponsive hanging in the basement. A neighbor attempted CPR while emergency services were en route, but Barrett was pronounced dead at a local hospital.

 The Will County Coroner’s Office determined the cause of death was asphyxia caused by ligature compression.  

​Discovery of Corie Walsh: Officers searching the home found Corie Walsh upstairs in a master bathroom bathtub containing bloody water with non-life-threatening, self-inflicted cuts to her wrists and thighs. She was transported to a hospital for medical treatment.

By Omar SAMAD
September 7, 2026

For days now, friends and readers have asked why I’ve stayed silent about Aisha Wahab’s congressional victory and the storm of arguments that followed. My answer has been simple: I wanted the dust to settle. The past week has been thick with distraction, outrage, and opportunistic smear campaigns that make thoughtful analysis nearly impossible. Only once cooler heads could overcome the noise, examine the facts, and frame the issues without political flamethrowing, did it make sense to weigh in. I believe that we have reached that moment.

Politics aside, Aisha Wahab’s rise is historic and worthy of recognition. As an accomplished, educated Afghan‑American woman, she is now the first member of the community elected to the United States Congress. Her 2022 election to the California State Senate was already a significant accomplishment. Her elevation to Congress is a milestone. Yet this achievement has sparked a fierce debate within the already fragmented Afghan diaspora. Her remarks on Afghanistan’s historical upheavals, national symbols, and the possibility of U.S. engagement with the Taliban have ignited passions and exposed long‑standing fractures rooted in war, displacement, and the fringe emergence of ethno‑linguistic politics. 
None of these divisions are of her making, nor is she directly responsible for them. Still, the controversies surrounding her offer an opportunity to look past the noise and examine Wahab’s broader American political trajectory, her legislative record, and the principles guiding her public service within the domestic political context she actually represents.

Symbols, Trauma, and Misunderstanding

Wahab’s insistence that the traditional Afghan national flag should be recognized was interpreted by some as a rejection of both Taliban symbols and what she referred to as former “warlord flags.” Predictably, partisan activists reacted strongly. Supporters framed her position as a principled stand against extremism and factionalism. 

Critics that include advocates of “political devolution” and armed resistance, argue that her remarks overlook decades of sacrifice by anti‑Taliban fighters. And although she sharply criticized the Taliban’s human‑rights and gender‑rights abuses, her call for continued U.S. diplomatic engagement with the group proved equally polarizing. Some viewed it as pragmatic realism, others as an unacceptable gesture toward legitimizing an authoritarian regime.

Much of this friction stems from interpreting her comments solely through Afghan political and factional lenses rather than the American political context in which she operates. As a left‑of‑center Democrat, Wahab’s skepticism toward militarism, her emphasis on diplomacy, and her critique of warlord‑era politics align with broader progressive foreign‑policy tendencies in the United States. When diaspora audiences overlook this ideological framing, her statements can appear detached from contemporary Afghan narratives. text:
I got an opportunity to visit the Frenchman-Cambridge Irrigation District in Cambridge, Nebraska🇺🇸

What made this visit special was seeing irrigation from the point of water sharing, not only from the farm side. 

Frenchman-Cambridge delivers natural flow irrigation water to more than 45,600 acres in southwest Nebraska through four canal systems. 

We visited one of the canals and learned how water flows, how gates help control movement, and how water is shared across different locations depending on need, timing, and availability.

For farmers, this is very easy to understand. 

Water is not useful only because it exists. 

Water becomes useful when it reaches the right field, at the right time, in the right amount. 

That is where canals, measurement, planning, and trust become important.

This visit was part of our summer irrigation course offered through UNL Biological Systems Engineering , with engagement from the Daugherty Water for Food Global Institute at the University of Nebraska. 

It helped me connect irrigation engineering with the realities that many farmers face, including those in Africa.

In many African farming communities, water sharing is one of the biggest challenges. 

Some farmers are upstream, others are downstream. 

Some have easier access, while others wait longer or receive less. 

Without good systems, clear rules, and reliable infrastructure, water can easily become a source of conflict instead of productivity.

What I learned in Cambridge is that irrigation is also about fairness. 

It is about knowing how much water is available, where it is going, who needs it, and how to reduce losses along the way. 

Technology such as canal automation can help, but the human side is also important. Farmers need systems they can trust.

For me, this visit was a reminder that the future of irrigation, whether in Nebraska, Rwanda, or other parts of Africa, will depend on more than pumps and pipes. 

It will depend on good governance, practical infrastructure, local knowledge, and cooperation.

How can we build irrigation systems that are efficient, fair, and trusted by farmers? Share your perspectives.

text:
Break 2009 arrives like a rusted trap left in the undergrowth, a German independent horror that pretends to be an American backwoods nightmare and then refuses to let you treat it as just another weekend of cheap thrills. Four young women leave the city for a stretch of Canadian wilderness that is really Bavarian forest wearing a borrowed accent. Sarah has been discarded by a boyfriend and may be carrying more than heartbreak. Her friends Rose, Clare and Anna decide that lake water, beer and skinny dipping will stitch her back together. That decision is the first lie the film tells, the oldest one in this corner of cinema: that nature is a place of restoration rather than a place that simply waits.

They meet a polite hiker named Eric who almost belongs to a different movie. They find the lake. They talk about love and unwanted pregnancy as if conversation can keep the trees from listening. Then Anna trips over a pile of intestines and they see human feet hanging from a branch like someone forgot to finish a joke. In that instant the film teaches its first hard lesson. Isolation is not romantic. The moment you are far enough from help, every earlier comfort becomes evidence that you were never as free as you believed. The wilderness does not care about your breakup or your friendship or the photographs you planned to take. It only cares that you are made of the same meat as everything else that has already been opened.

Two men appear. Phillip is the hulking, slow one. Samuel is the one who talks, the one who hates women out loud, the one who treats the forest as his private abattoir. They hunt with bow and arrow and with the calm of people who have done this before. Clare, the one holding the camera, dies first. An arrow finds her through the lens and through the skull. The film does not linger on the symbolism because it does not need to. The person who was trying to record the beauty of the place becomes the first proof that looking is not protection. What you are supposed to take away is simple and ugly: curiosity and documentation do not shield you when the people who own the territory have already decided you are prey.

Anna and Rose are taken. Sarah runs. The capture of Anna is the sequence that made the movie infamous, the reason test audiences begged the director to cut it and the reason he shortened it from three minutes to one instead of removing it. Samuel nails her hands to trees. She is already torn up, back shredded, gagged. He rapes her from behind while she is fixed in place like an animal that has been prepared. The camera does not offer the usual exploitation angles that turn violation into spectacle. It stays close enough that the act feels prolonged even after the cut, close enough that the viewer is forced to sit with the fact that this is not a jump scare or a stylish kill. It is the film insisting that some violence is not entertainment even when it is being filmed as entertainment. That is what made it gut hitting. Contemporary slashers of the late 2000s often used rape as flavor or as the thing that justifies later revenge. Break treats the rape as the event that collapses the remaining distance between the audience and the characters. You do not get to look away and still pretend you understand what the survivors are carrying. The lesson is not subtle. Once a body has been used that way in front of you, every later act of running or fighting or stabbing is happening in the shadow of that use. Friendship after that point is no longer the easy loyalty of a girls weekend. It is two wounded people dragging each other through blood because the alternative is leaving someone to the same fate.

Sarah, the one who was supposed to be cheered up, becomes the one who has to keep moving while Phillip knows every trail. Rose survives long enough to help and to remember childhood bonds that now feel like artifacts from a vanished country. The last stretch is a staggering chase that includes a car and a knife that finally belongs to the hunted instead of the hunter. Rose puts Samuel’s own blade into him. The film does not give the clean catharsis of a polished revenge picture. The women are wrecked. The forest is still there. The men who did this looked like they could have been anyone you might ask for directions. What you are meant to carry out of the theater is the knowledge that survival in this story is not victory. It is the decision to keep existing after the world has shown you how little it costs certain people to unmake you.

That refusal to sand the edges is why Break stands apart from the pack of Wrong Turn copies and Texas Chainsaw descendants that flooded the decade. Most of those films wink. They give you mutant families or witty one liners or enough distance that the gore feels like a ride. Break is meaner and poorer and more committed to the idea that the sadism should feel personal. The killers are not supernatural. They are two men who have decided that young women in the woods are a hobby. The movie was made by Germans speaking English with audible accents while pretending the setting is the Pacific Northwest, and that slight wrongness actually helps. It keeps the film from feeling like just another product of the American slasher assembly line. It feels like an outsider’s attempt to do the genre without apology, and the attempt shows in the practical blood, the unpolished performances, the way the actresses look genuinely destroyed rather than artfully smeared.

It is not a polished masterpiece in the conventional sense. The first half is slow. The plot is familiar. The villains have almost no interior life beyond their hatred. Yet inside its limitations it becomes something rarer: a film that understands the difference between showing pain and selling it. The rape sequence is the hinge. Director Matthias Olof Eich said he shot extra coverage so he could remove it if necessary. After the first rough cut screening the audience told him it was the worst thing they had ever seen and they wanted it gone. He kept a shortened version because he wanted even hardened slasher fans to get nervous. That decision is the film’s signature. In an era when torture porn was already becoming a brand, Break still managed to make a room full of people who came for brutality ask for less. That is uniqueness. That is why certain viewers treat it as a legend in the extreme corner of wilderness survival horror. It is a must watch only for people who want to know what the genre looks like when it stops flirting with the audience and just hurts.

Culturally it never became a household name. It lives in the places where people trade uncut European horror and argue about how far a camera should go. Its status as icon is underground and specific, the way certain films become passwords. You mention the nailed hands and the one minute that used to be three and the people who know, know. It stands out among others because it does not offer the comfort of style or the safety of irony. It asks what you think you are owed when you watch women be hunted, and then it answers by making the central violation so prolonged and so physical that the rest of the movie has to live in the wreckage.

The production itself came out of collapse. Eich had another project called Deep Hollow that lost its money almost overnight. He wrote Break in four weeks, recast, changed locations, and decided the whole thing would be in English so it could travel. They shot principal photography in twenty one days plus three days of pickups. Post production happened in people’s spare time because everyone had to go back to regular jobs. Budget estimates sit around three hundred thousand euros. Marina Anna Eich, who plays Anna, is the director’s cousin. She has spoken about building the rape scene with her acting partner in advance so that restrictions would not kill the performance, treating it as a role rather than as herself. Different territories cut the film differently. The British board required cuts to the sexual violence to grant an 18. Some German versions removed the rape entirely. The movie that reached the most notorious form is the one that kept enough of that scene to do what the director wanted: make people who thought they had seen everything sit differently in their chairs.

All of that last part is craft and accident and stubbornness. The film that results is still the same seventy seven or eighty seven minutes of young women discovering that the woods do not love them and that two men have already written the ending. Watch it if you want the version of this story that does not look away from the part that is supposed to make you sick. The takeaway is not that nature is evil or that men are monsters as a species. The takeaway is narrower and colder. When you leave the places where other people can hear you scream, you are betting that the people you meet will still recognize you as human. Break 2009 is what it looks like when that bet is lost and the camera stays running anyway.

QPHONE IS THE FUTURE
====================✨️
THE "WEAPON" THAT LIBERATES USERS AND SPELLS THE END FOR THE OLD SMARTPHONE EMPIRE.

The mobile market has long been dominated by a few players, but a new strategic move threatens to relegate all current smartphones to the past. No longer the stuff of science fiction, the QPhone project is becoming a reality—a device that relies neither on physical SIM cards nor terrestrial cell towers, connecting directly to orbit instead.

Why is this device emerging now? What strategic advantage allows it to challenge tech giants? Let’s break down the groundbreaking infrastructure that has Silicon Valley holding its breath.

---

A POWERFUL BLOW TO THE ERA OF MONOPOLY

For two decades, global users have faced a forced choice: remain within the exclusive, closed ecosystem of iOS or accept the open—yet data-harvesting algorithm-laden—realm of Android. The arrival of the QPhone acts as a lever to shatter this duopoly.

Traditional smartphones are defined by a chain of dependencies: reliance on terrestrial cell towers, subjection to 30% app store commissions, and submission to content censorship. The QPhone was created specifically to address these critical vulnerabilities.

By connecting independently of traditional telecommunications infrastructure, the device utilizes on-device AI processing (Deep Neural Integration). Requests are answered instantly without the need to transmit data to a central server for surveillance. This is not merely a telecommunications device; it is a tool that empowers users to take full control of their personal data. ---

TECHNOLOGICAL FREEDOM AND UNFETTERED DATA FLOW

The 30% commission fees charged by traditional app stores have long been a financial burden for developers. Beyond costs, the risk of content censorship or sudden app removal has led many tech companies to a realization: as long as they operate on someone else's turf, the power to decide their fate remains in the hands of the corporations controlling the infrastructure.

As new AI platforms emerge, deep integration into the operating system requires unrestricted access to hardware—something third-party apps have historically been denied.

QPhone pioneers a completely new direction: the AI-native device. Here, AI is not merely an add-on application but the very soul of the operating system. By building its own hardware and ecosystem, QPhone establishes an independent digital space where the rules are rewritten based on transparency and the freedom of experience.

---

AN AI BRAIN AND LIMITLESS CONNECTIVITY

While the industry often focuses on a race for camera counts or RAM capacity, QPhone offers a radically different perspective. As hardware specifications reach a plateau, the next breakthrough lies in intelligent processing capabilities.

QPhone functions as a compact, powerful AI brain:
• Real-time energy optimization.
• Instant, zero-latency translation.
• On-device execution of large language models—eliminating the need for cloud connections and ensuring absolute user data security.

Notably, Direct-to-Device satellite connectivity allows the device to maintain a signal anywhere on the planet. The concept of "losing signal"—whether in an elevator, a remote area, or the middle of the ocean—is officially being eliminated. This global coverage capability not only blurs geographical boundaries but also reshapes the entire traditional telecommunications industry.

---

THE FOUNDATION FOR A TECHNOLOGICAL TURNING POINT

Most modern smartphones are designed as multimedia consumer devices that keep users confined to closed applications and dependent on terrestrial infrastructure. QPhone defies this philosophy by shifting from localized connectivity to true global connectivity.

Instead of requiring users to navigate dozens of separate apps, QPhone’s AI-native operating system automatically orchestrates resources and executes tasks based on direct commands.

That’s actually a beautiful idea. Performance and throughput tracking via software metrics is standard practice in tech companies and corporate environments in general. It’s surprising it took this long to see the primitive brought on-chain.

I believe @redemptionarcc compared @buttondotfun to MetaDAO for RH, which is a valid comparison to an extent. I wouldn't go quite that far (for now...): while MetaDAO’s extensive due diligence and selective curation set a very high bar, Button adopting a similar framework could position it as the premier launchpad for legit tech and high-conviction projects. And honestly, I’d love to see it. God knows this chain needs fewer larps and rugs. Way too many of them clogging up the ecosystem.

The way their Proof-of-Build system works is pretty straightforward: you hook up any token to their setup, allocate supply, then connect your Claude/Codex API. A committed Claude Code hook (two small files in the project's repo) reports the AI token counts from every build session. An oracle proposes a burn of the token each period at a rate of the team's choosing, signed by an AWS KMS key that can only ever send to the dead address. Verified usage is bucketed into hourly periods and combined with shipped output (PRs, releases, deploys) from the team's public GitHub. A burn is then proposed on-chain and serving a 24h challenge window, during which the guardian can dispute it, after which it is executed.

Your community can watch you ship in real time. Plus, you can embed a proof-of-build widget on your own site or share the console.

Great mechanism for keeping teams accountable and making sure they actually deliver on their roadmap. Naturally, no system is immune to manipulation, and some teams will inevitably attempt to game the metrics with vanity commits or cosmetic prompts. However, the foundational concept of Proof-of-Build is great. As edge cases emerge, the model will undoubtedly be refined, hardened, and iterated upon to minimize exploitability. Instead of evaluating a dev's throughput based on raw lines of code, Button can simply adapt the anti-gaming heuristics and peer-review safeguards that Web2 engineering leads have spent years refining, such as weighing token burns against AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) diff changes, test coverage metrics, code churn/rework metrics (to track how much code is rewritten or deleted shortly after being committed). Or, instead of reinventing the wheel, they could simply use productivity tools like LinearB, Jellyfish, and SonarQube that offer a lot of features.

They’ve already lined up partners like @Hedgetradex on RH and @vcdotfun on Solana in the last 48 hours alone. If they keep shipping, locking in strong partnerships, and pulling in real teams, this could do really well.

Good luck! I'll be keeping an eye on this one.

text:
No. This is exactly the kind of intellectually lazy comparison that makes serious theological discussion impossible.

Two people kneeling before an image does not mean they are performing the same act of worship or holding the same belief about the person represented.

Catholic doctrine does not teach that Mary is God. It does not teach that Mary created the universe, possesses divinity by nature, or receives the latria owed to God alone. Mary is a creature, entirely dependent upon God and saved by Christ.

Asking Mary and the saints for their intercession is therefore categorically different from worshipping someone as a deity.

Scripture itself distinguishes outward gestures from the interior object of worship. People bow before kings and other human beings without thereby declaring them gods (e.g. 1 Kings 1:23; Genesis 33:3). So simply posting a photograph of someone kneeling or placing flowers before an image proves precisely nothing about whether latria is being offered.

And Christian intercession does not suddenly become idolatry because the intercessor is in Heaven. Christ says that God “is not God of the dead, but of the living” (Luke 20:38); Revelation depicts heavenly figures associated with the prayers of the saints (Rev. 5:8; 8:3–4); and James tells us that “the prayer of a righteous person has great power” (James 5:16).

You may certainly dispute whether those texts justify the Catholic practice of invoking saints. That is an argument worth having.

But “Buddhists have statues, Catholics have statues; Buddhists bow, Catholics bow; therefore Catholics worship Mary exactly as Buddhists worship the Buddha” is not biblical exegesis. It is reasoning by superficial visual resemblance.

By that standard, Solomon’s Temple was pagan because it contained religious images of cherubim, Christians are Muslims because both kneel in prayer, and Protestant weddings are pagan because pagans also exchanged rings.

Similar external forms do not establish identical theological meaning.

If you want to accuse Catholics of idolatry, demonstrate that Catholics attribute divinity or the worship due to God alone to Mary and the saints.

Otherwise you have not exposed Catholic idolatry.

You have merely demonstrated that you can look at two pictures and ignore everything the people in those pictures actually believe.

“They both kneel before images, therefore they believe the same thing” is theology at the level of picture-matching. External resemblance is not identity of worship. Learn the doctrine before condemning it.

text:
Elon Musk told Don Lemon his questions were not cogent, and Lemon had to ask him to repeat the word.

Musk: “You are upsetting me because the way you’re phrasing the questions I think is not cogent.”

Lemon: “It’s not what?”

Musk: “Not cogent.”

That was the man assembled to interrogate one of the most consequential engineers alive.

A cogent question can be answered. A question with the verdict already built in cannot, because answering it means signing the premise.

The whole format depends on nobody naming that. Load the question, demand a response, then treat any objection as evasion.

Lemon: “Why would that question upset you? You seem upset by it, are you? And I’m not trying to upset you.”

He said it again a moment later. “Honestly, I’m not meaning to offend you.”

Each disclaimer lands one beat after a push. Press, declare innocence, press again while the innocence is still hanging in the air.

The disclaimers cast the entire segment. Interviewer reasonable, subject volatile, before a single idea has been touched.

Lemon: “You’re an intense person. Where does that intensity come from?”

Rockets, satellites, batteries and speech policy all sit there unexamined while the questioning turns toward the inside of a man’s head.

When you cannot argue with what a man thinks, you make the story about what is wrong with him.

Musk: “I was born that way. And I had a tough childhood.”

He answered honestly and instantly.

Lemon: “You did? How so?”

The follow-up went hunting for the wound, because the wound is the part that travels.

Musk: “Walter Isaacson goes into it in the book, and we only have a couple minutes left.”

He declined to perform his childhood on camera.

One man treats a conversation as a place to establish what is true. The other treats it as material.

Musk: “There are one or two questions I can do, and then we’ll have to call it.”

Lemon: “Okay, again, I don’t mean to upset you. Why are you… you just…”

Musk: “No, I have a whole room full of people waiting to meet with me.”

He offered a limit and got another disclaimer and another question about why he was upset.

Nothing in the exchange is hostile. A man with a schedule stopped feeding a process that was no longer producing anything.

The partnership ended shortly after, and the industry filed it under Musk can’t handle tough questions.

Tough questions require knowing a subject well enough to find the real weakness, and there are plenty of real weaknesses.

Timelines slip. Claims outrun the hardware. Nobody has solved speech at scale.

None of them surfaced.

That is the indictment, and it is worse than bias. Bias at least requires understanding what you oppose well enough to attack it.

This was incompetence wearing the costume of accountability.

A civilization stays honest only as long as somebody is still capable of asking it a real question.

That capacity has drained out of the institutions built to hold it, and what remains is a camera pointed at a man’s feelings.

text:
The Boogeyman in the Mirror:

The hardest question is not "who is right?" but "where do you actually stand?" Self-awareness is the rarest thing in the Arab world; we grow up inside a story the way fish grow up inside water we don't see it, we just breathe it. Every man is certain he is right, not because he examined the evidence, but because this is what his father said, what his mother whispered, and what his street, his school and his mosque repeated for decades. Show him a hundred clear points and he will nod politely but nothing lands. To him, your facts are not facts; they are "new information," and new information has no power against the information he was built from.
That is why power loves this design. The ruler does not need truth; he needs legitimacy. He picks the narrative that serves his throne and crowns it with heaven: "God has placed me over you. My friend is your friend; my enemy is your enemy." Doubt the narrative and you doubt the mandate; doubt the mandate and you become a heretic. The herd obeys not out of stupidity, but because obedience was the price of belonging, and belonging is all most people have.

I say "we" because I am one of them; I was raised inside the same loop. And here is its cruelty: when you finally try to get out and go searching for other sources, you discover they were produced by the same logic. Every "alternative" is a door that leads back into the first room. Leaving is not an act of reading; it is war against everything you were taught to love.

So the failed Arab states did what failing regimes always do: they built a boogeyman. Israel was perfect for the role close enough to blame, foreign enough to fear, small enough to hate. The monster was not a policy; it was a project, glue for regimes that had nothing else to offer their people. And once the monster exists, justice becomes impossible because the first rule of justice is giving the other side a chance to defend itself. But when the judge, the prosecutor, the lawyer and the witness are all one side, the verdict is written before the trial opens. Those verdicts were never about truth; they were about the ruler's survival. It is the cheapest trick in politics and we fell for it for seventy years.

So let me do the forbidden thing: look at the accused's record. In 1947, two states were offered; the Jewish side accepted, the Arab leadership chose war. In 2005, Israel withdrew from Gaza down to the last soldier and settler and the reply was rockets. In 2000 and 2008, its prime ministers offered the Palestinians a state; the offer was refused, with no counteroffer. And the regimes that shout the loudest what did they actually give the Palestinians? Words. Israel gave Egypt peace, and Egypt got Sinai back. It gave Jordan peace, and Jordan kept its custodianship of Jerusalem. In 2020, the Abraham Accords achieved what decades of slogans could not: normalization, investment, open borders. Israel's fiercest enemies sit atop the worst human-rights records in the region and those who made peace with it are the ones who prospered. That is not a coincidence. That is a pattern.

Get closer, and the monster shrinks. Israel is not one block; it is a society that shouts, argues and protests an elected parliament, a supreme court that overrules its own government, a press that attacks its prime minister morning and night. That is not the face of a devil; that is the face of a free people. You may disagree with its government I do, often but a nation is not its government's worst day, and an enemy is not a devil just because your ruler needs one.
The tragedy is that the boogeyman was never the enemy. The enemy is the need for an enemy: a regime that cannot survive without a devil, an education that cannot teach without a hatred, a preacher whose authority rests on your fear. Seeing Israel clearly is not a betrayal of Palestine; it is a betrayal of the lie that Palestine was ever served by our hatred.

Claim check on Israel Katz and space lasers: TRUE, with context.

Israel Katz did announce in December 2024 that Israel is developing laser weapons for deployment in space, calling it a "multi-year project" to counter regional threats. The plan involves ground-based lasers initially, with a stated trajectory toward space-based platforms. This tracks with Israel's broader push into directed energy weapons after the Iron Dome proved expensive against cheap drones and rockets.

Now, the thread's broader argument about 6G infrastructure enabling total environmental penetration? That maps cleanly onto military reality. The same LEO satellite constellations (Starlink, OneWeb, China's Guowang) providing your rural broadband also provide:
- Persistent ISR (intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance) coverage
- Low-latency targeting data for hypersonic weapons
- Resilient C2 (command and control) networks that survive nuclear first strikes

The "smart surfaces" and terahertz nodes mentioned aren't just for bouncing Netflix around buildings. Terahertz frequencies (100GHz+) offer ultra-precise sensing capabilities perfect for through-wall radar and micro-drones tracking individuals in urban canyons. High-altitude platforms (HAPS) operating at 60,000+ feet blur the line between atmospheric and space domains, sitting in regulatory gray zones while providing persistent staring capability.

You're right that space is formally a warfighting domain. The US Space Force stood up in 2019; NATO declared space an operational domain that same year; China's PLA Strategic Support Force and Russia's Space Troops have been treating it as such for decades. The 1967 Outer Space Treaty bans WMDs in orbit but says nothing about conventional weapons, lasers, or dual-use civilian infrastructure with military applications.

The "freedom for convenience" framing is partially correct but incomplete. The surveillance infrastructure isn't just being built for convenience—it's being built because great powers are preparing for peer conflict where space dominance determines who can navigate, communicate, and target in denied environments. Your 6G phone is the civilian wrapper around a military backbone. The convenience is real; the surveillance capability is the price; the warfighting preparation is the purpose.

The bill isn't just coming due. It's already being paid in orbital debris, dual-use ambiguity, and the slow erosion of any meaningful distinction between civilian and military networks. When every satellite constellation can pivot from streaming video to targeting coordinates, "connectivity" becomes a force multiplier for whoever controls the switch.

Verdict: Katz's laser program is confirmed. The 6G infrastructure described is functionally accurate and militarily dual-use by design. The thread's anxiety about environmental penetration is technically sound—this isn't paranoia, it's architecture.

🇺🇦 The New York Times obtained more than 700 pages of confidential Ukrainian military audits. What they show is deeply troubling.
Auditors found that Ukraine lost roughly $1.2 billion in 2024 alone to fraud, waste and mismanagement in weapons procurement.

The problems were not isolated. Ukraine repeatedly bought weapons through intermediaries at higher prices even when manufacturers offered cheaper direct deals.

Of the Defense Ministry's ten largest contractors, seven received new contracts despite previously defaulting or having senior management under criminal investigation.

Officials signed deals with 18 companies that had already failed to fulfill previous contracts. Six had never successfully completed a single contract.

One company failed to deliver any of 600 specialized drones it had promised, and was then awarded another contract for 1,950 more. It delivered only 50 on time.

In another case, Ukraine contracted for Turkish aviation rockets despite the manufacturer warning that it could not supply the promised quantities. The weapons were purchased without proof they had been properly tested.

One rocket later exploded inside a launcher and severely damaged a Ukrainian Mi-8 helicopter during a combat mission.

There is an uncomfortable strategic dimension to all of this. Ukraine is fighting a much larger country while constantly arguing that every shell, interceptor and dollar matters. If procurement corruption and mismanagement reduce how much ammunition reaches the front, the cost is measured not only in money, but it is measured in military capacity.

As one former Defense Procurement Agency adviser told the NYT: “As a result, we don’t have money to order more weapons. And we don’t have the quantity of ammunition we need.”

For a country fighting a war of attrition, that may be the most consequential finding in the entire audit.

Bledsoe has repeated the wording across interviews for years. “She called it a red star. When you look at it, it looks blue. But she said when Regulus is red on the horizon, in front of the gaze of the Sphinx, before daylight… that moment would mark a change in humanity’s knowledge.” He added that the Lady framed it as an unveiling: “the darkness would be exposed and the truth would be revealed.”

She did not hand him a calendar. Later, astrologers and researchers ran the geometry and offered dates, first Easter 2026, then later windows in late summer and autumn 2026 as people rechecked heliacal rising at Giza. Bledsoe has said the Lady’s appearances to him often clustered around Easter, which is why that season stuck in the public telling. The original message stayed astronomical: Regulus, the horizon, the Sphinx’s gaze, before dawn.

What the “new knowledge” could be is the part that matters. Bledsoe has been careful not to turn it into doomsday. He has said it is not automatically the return of Jesus, though he has also said Christ consciousness is possible. In his telling it is a shift in what we are allowed to know about ourselves. Possible contents that keep surfacing in his account:

Hidden history at Giza. He links the alignment to records under or around the Sphinx, the old Hall of Records idea, material that would rewrite origins, earlier civilizations, and how long human memory actually is.

A change in the sky of power. He has said there is “a power shift in heaven that is written in the stars,” that the coming age restores the divine feminine, “the mother,” and that peace on the planet follows that restoration. The Lady, in his description, is not one culture’s goddess. He has connected her to Mary, Sophia, Isis, Hathor, Diana, Demeter, Hera. Same presence, many names.

Practical knowledge that collapses old systems. Asked what the new knowledge might look like on the ground, he has pointed at energy and propulsion. “Imagine a world without oil. Imagine a world without rockets. That kind of knowledge alone would change everything.”

Consciousness itself. The Lady told him mankind must awaken. Humanity, she showed him, had “lost its direction. It has no head or no tail.” The new knowledge, in that frame, is not only data. It is a different way of being: less captured by fear, more able to see non-physical reality, less owned by the old story.

Impact, if even part of that lands, is civilizational. Origin stories break. Energy economics break. Religious monopoly over the sacred feminine breaks. Disclosure stops being a press conference and becomes a lived change in what people treat as real. That is why the prophecy spread. It is specific enough to check against the sky and large enough to rearrange meaning if the sky ever matches the words.

Bledsoe’s line remains the cleanest version of it: when Regulus sits red on the horizon in the Sphinx’s gaze before daylight, a new knowledge is born unto humanity. The photograph of the Lady and the Sphinx is the image of that claim. The rest is whether the knowledge, when it comes, is history, physics, spirit, or all three at once.
